translations.text: The Interpretation of the Song of Songs, spoken by the blessed Hippolytus.
1.1. Solomon had wisdom, but he was not himself Wisdom; he found grace from God, but he was not himself that Grace; he was the son of David, but he was not himself Christ. 1.2.
It was granted him by God to utter three books in the world, and he reveals something of the power of these three books under the guidance of the Holy Spirit,
for by the teaching of grace that word was found, and by dwelling with wisdom he came to have a share from God. 1.3.
He assigns a certain threefold division, for these three books were uttered by the will of the Holy Spirit, and from that blessed mouth by the Holy Spirit.
For it is the Holy Spirit who was proclaiming the Trinity, so that the grace of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit might be declared. 1.4.
For first, by wisdom, he utters the Proverbs, through which the wondrous and unrevealed grace of the Father is declared,
and, among the books, Ecclesiastes, in which he showed us obscured things by that word of knowledge, for it was the Son.
Third, in the unity of the Holy Spirit he sets forth something, the Song which the Holy Spirit was teaching to many. 1.5.
Now these three became a book of unity, and the third was by the sealing of the Holy Spirit,
for first the Father, wondrous, and the riches uttered from wisdom; the earth [?], the Ecclesiastes of what is dark, uttered to the world by the Son through proclamation and obscure understanding.
The third is the Song: for the gladdening of the Holy Spirit and for the delight of consolation, and the knowledge of God was made manifest to many. 1.6.
Now, having been made worthy of that grace, he speaks by the hand of the Holy Spirit: "This is he who created all these things."
Not that he himself was this one, but he was a hearer, and was taught all these things by him, being with him, for the Word was crying out through him,
for he himself was Wisdom, and he was showing us that which the Father wills to bestow on the prophets who exist through that Word;
he was not without a share of this Wisdom, yet he was not himself Wisdom, and wisdom was trained along with him.
It is she who said: "Before all the mountains I was begotten."
Now that Wisdom was begotten by the Father before all the mountains, and by that Wisdom the beauty of this world was ordered. 1.7.
For thus Wisdom, through the manifold grace of the Father, was showing us its adornment by the command of the Father.
To this same world, through dwelling together with that Wisdom, he says with reference to Solomon: "I, Wisdom, have dwelt with you, counsel and knowledge."
Now knowledge granted to believers tells us the will, by the counsel of the Father. 1.8.
Now this Wisdom was none other than Christ, and Christ is the Son. And that this is so, the apostle Paul testifies, saying:
"If we preach Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God." 1.9.
Now this Wisdom is spoken from the mouth of the blessed Solomon, uttering the good grace, the gift of the Spirit, a new song.
For he was singing a new song, by announcing the counsel of revelation, whence it is to be understood,
what was afterwards going to be said, the words of which that writer writes down beforehand by uttering figures and songs. 1.10.
For it is said of him that three thousand parables and five thousand songs were uttered by him, and from the cedars of Lebanon as far as the plants
that are even on the roofs, and about birds and beasts and creeping things that move upon the earth. 1.11.
And where is all this very great knowledge? Or where is the counsel spoken over so long a time?
Has it been hidden, or is there anyone who could have uttered this? Where are those books? For these Proverbs are only a small part of what was spoken in wisdom;
there is also another book, Ecclesiastes, arranged in seven and eight [?] sections, and the Song of Songs, which amounts to no more than three songs. 1.12.
Now it seems as if all those books have perished. But if that scripture should appear false to anyone, let it not be so!
Rather, much of these writings was lacking, for which reason that clear bestowal of grace was to take place for certain reasons [?].
And he wrote the song beforehand. By these he makes known these many songs ordained beforehand, 1.13.
for he says in Kingdoms that he uttered five thousand parables. But here he gives assurance [?] that as for the Song of Songs, which alone he mentions,
the 'Song of Songs' signifies to us that he had five thousand collected with him, and he set them forth clearly in this one.
Now upon that clear disclosure the power also follows, and those things that belonged to the old [writing]
he selected by the Spirit for every need, and those which alike are tributary to the church by [?], this then became something to be understood. 1.14.
But so that we may know the scrupulous care concerning this word, see with all ability and vividly what has been uttered from those writings, and the things not mentioned in those Proverbs.
For that scripture speaks thus among the books: "These are the untested proverbs of Solomon, which the friends of King Hezekiah selected."
And that selection took place after the death of Solomon.
Now from where are these unexamined proverbs of Solomon, which the friends of King Hezekiah examined?
From where, if not from those books in which it speaks of three thousand parables? That is, some of them were made known from the accounts of those friends of Hezekiah,
who were wise; they afterwards sought out certain things and added them to those old selected ones for the edification of the church. 1.15.

And the reason for this too appears [?] for the sake of disclosure: for some things were set aside as outside, and some were shown to be needful, so that through these there might be edification for whoever is able to hear. 1.16.

Now concerning those things that existed, what has fallen lies in the midst alone [?]; but there is some other ancient, spiritual account, for the account of those things that have grown old is incumbent on those who are able to recount in faith.
Now the Spirit sings what is ordained in the churches, for it shows us in various ways the division of figures,
which it is incumbent on us to recount to those who are able in faith to hear.
2.1. Now let us come to this and see what this passage set before us says: "Kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your breasts are more beautiful than wine."
"And the fragrance of your ointment is above all spices. And like the fragrance of ointment your name is poured out." 2.2.
What, then, is the will of the Spirit, toward which this power is directed, or what might be the sign of this thought?
We must also make known to those who listen that this is the figure of the people who entreat the heavenly Word,
that he may kiss them, for mouth desires to touch mouth, for the power of the Spirit desires to join itself to its own. 2.3.
And it says: "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth," which means this very thing:
Make me worthy through the commandments which he commands, this one having been brought in to me [?], for from that mouth comes love.
For it says: "Your breasts are better to me than wine."
For just as wine gladdens the heart, so the commandments of Christ gladden; for like infants
who suck at the breasts to draw out milk, so also all who draw the commandments from the Law and the Gospel obtain everlasting food,
for the breast of Christ is nothing other than the two laws, and this milk is nothing other than the commandments of the law.
Now suck the milk from those breasts, that you may be built up and be a perfect witness, 2.4. for it says: "Your breasts are more desirable than wine.
And the fragrance of your ointment is beyond blended spices."
But now what is this fragrant ointment of Christ, if not the Word, since that Word is rightly reckoned above spices?
For just as blended spices give forth fragrance, so also the Word who came forth from the Father gladdens those who listen [?]. 2.5.
"The fragrance of ointment poured out is your name." O new distinction, and of the wonderful thoughts proclaimed by the Holy Spirit!
For was it not enough to say "Your name is ointment of fragrance"? But instead it says "Ointment of fragrance poured out is your name."
For just as a vessel in which perfumed ointment is kept, so long as it remains closed up and sealed, does not let out its fragrance, yet it has it, and its potency is there,
but when it is opened, it gives forth its fragrance and fills those near it and those far away, so also the Word was in the heart of the Father.
And so long as he had not yet come forth, he gladdened no one.
But when the Father sent forth that breath of fragrance, the Word spread gladness to all. 2.6.
O the beauty of this fragrance, which has spread forth so as to fill the world! Therefore it says: "Ointment of fragrance poured out is your name."
For that jar of joy was opened, which is the Father's mouth, by the bringing forth of the precious Word from it.
This fragrance he sends down from heaven. This, having come down, filled all;
through this all the praise of the prophets was filled, and all the righteous carried it away, and the plunderers snatched it,
gathering the good thing together in their souls, that all might be filled with the fragrance together. 2.7.
Now learn, O man, what is set forth here and what is ordained here: for the fragrance of the ointment from the Father is Christ for us.
For when you were living in paganism, no one brought reproach upon you.
But now that the word of holiness has been brought before you and you have been taught by Christ, so that you might at once become a disciple,
very quickly that ointment of yours was offered, spread abroad, and made manifest for labors.
Everything was at once stirred up against you, for it was a scent that seemed a heaviness: to some it was heavy, and some it gladdened,
for the strength of that fragrant ointment was oppressive, yet some it gladdened, for it made the faithful of God obedient and convicted the disobedient. 2.8.
"A scent of fragrance poured out is your name." Behold the fragrance of that ointment poured out.
It was poured into the womb, and it created a new man, born; it was poured upon the waters, and it sanctified the waters;
it spread among the Gentiles, and it gathered the Gentiles; it spread over Israel, but those who were unbelieving did not receive that fragrance;
now that counsel spread among Israel, and the Gentiles who believed in it gathered.
Therefore this word must be carefully heeded: he does not speak thus, "ointment spilled," but "ointment poured forth,"
by its being spread in various ways over many; for what is spilled is held in contempt, but what is spread does not run short even in the vessel, and it fills those who are near.
Such is the nature of this ointment. O beloved, it is a spring of the Gospel, ever flowing forth, and it does not itself run short. 2.9.
Bring a vessel, O man, and come, draw near, so that you may be able to be filled with that ointment.
Receive this precious ointment. Do not sell it for three hundred drachmas, but anoint yourself with it without price.
Do not become like Judas, so that you may not grieve, but pour Christ upon your head through faith, so that you may be a fellow-heir. 2.10.
This ointment gladdened the righteous. Noah, loving it, was justified and was saved by the ark. 2.11.
Ham, despising it, exposed the shame of his father. 2.12.
Gladdened by it, the blessed Eber did not follow those who devised the work of the tower. 2.13.
Nimrod, despising it, prepared food for those who assailed God. 2.14.
Desiring it, the blessed Abraham hastened to come from the land of the Chaldeans to that dwelling place. 2.15.
Desiring it, the blessed Isaac wished the offering of himself for the sake of the world. 2.16.
Heedful for its sake, the blessed Jacob took hold of Esau's heel. 2.17.
Esau, despising it, was parted from the birthright, for he [?] it for the sake of food. 2.18.
The blessed Tamar set her heart on seizing it, and she showed herself as a harlot to Judah.
This the [?] of the child saw and marvelled, for on that child lay a purple-coloured mark, and she said: "How then was a way found for you through that wall?"
2.19. This the blessed Joseph loved, and he became patient when he was sold into Egypt.
Because of this he did not wish to embrace [her], and did not take upon himself the [?] of the queen, so as to be corrupted with corruption.
For the sake of this ointment Joseph learned patience, and he appeared as ruler over the Egyptians. 2.20.
For this the blessed Moses became zealous; he himself became an avenger and a ruler over Israel. 2.21.
Desiring this, the blessed Aaron was anointed priest. This vengeance the blessed Phinehas pursued, and with a spear he ran through the harlot and Zimri. 2.22.
Desiring this, in expectation, the blessed Joshua son of Nun took his stand as servant to Moses.
Now see, O men, the praise of all the righteous, how they desired this, this fragrant ointment;
O the blessed Joshua son of Nun, who showed from the new [?] of stone how he might reveal that ointment.
Desiring this, the blessed Joshua son of Nun circumcised the sons of Israel a second time with stone. 2.23.
This the blessed David loved. For this reason he came forth born from the heart of the Father.
And what then is the figure given by God concerning this blessed David, that "I have found a man, David, among the sons of Jesse, according to the will of my heart"?
What then does it mean to say, or what is its interpretation? O men, see now: the Father spoke beautifully, and most beautifully, for:
"Just as the Word came forth from my heart, in the same way from David too that Man shall come forth."
For he says: "I have found David, a man of my heart; my own heart has begotten the Word, and from David the Man."
O [?] of David, the righteous man, who was mingled with the heart of the Father!
Now from this very point the great counsel of this ointment is declared by him. 2.24. Desiring this, the blessed Solomon inherited eternal wisdom.
See, O men, the praises of the righteous, who in succession received the Holy Spirit as an ointment. 2.25.
The blessed Daniel, desiring this ointment, was also saved in the pit of lions. 2.26.
Ananias, Azarias and Misael, in their desire for this same ointment, longed to be anointed. Because of this they appeared as four in the furnace.
For it was that ointment which came down like dew upon the earth. 2.27.
Desiring this ointment, the blessed Joseph became a fellow-counsellor of God. 2.28.
Desiring this ointment, the blessed virgin Mary received the Word in her womb. 2.29.
O new and true counsels of the righteous, to whom it was shown!
This ointment Martha eagerly carried, who with all supplication and consolation sprinkled it upon Christ. 2.30.
This ointment Judas hated. And he sold Christ for thirty drachmas, because of which he said, crying out: "Why was there this waste of this ointment?
It was worth being sold for three hundred drachmas." 2.31. This saying shows us some type, O men. Now who was that ointment, if not Christ himself?
Does not that price, by means of those drachmas, foretell to us in advance the sufferings? For the sufferings he was found sold for thirty drachmas.
For it was indeed fitting for the truth that it be sold at a cheap price, so that the poor too might be able to obtain it easily.
So it was, beloved. 2.32. And from this that great counsel is revealed to us. Therefore it says: "Your name is an ointment of fragrance poured forth," it says.
"Therefore the young maidens have loved you and have clothed themselves." 2.33. Who are they who have loved you, if not the churches?
Or who are they who have breathed in, if not the churches, the faith from heaven above, so that "my fragrance may spread over you"? 2.34.
"Therefore the maidens have loved you. They have put you on by following your track; let us hasten after the track of the fragrance of your ointments,"
for by the breathing in of Christ it was proper to follow swiftly in his track. "Following after the fragrance of your ointments, let us hasten." 2.35.
Follow Christ, listen to the commandments, conduct yourself by what has been ordained, bind yourself to those summits [?], so that this desire of yours may be restrained!
3.1. "The king has brought me into his treasuries." And who is that king, if not Christ himself?
Or what are those treasuries, if not the royal things? This the people said: 3.2. "Let us rejoice and be glad in you," for he has ordained this for all.
First it tells us of the things that have been, then it reveals concerning the things to come at the time of repentance:
"Let us rejoice and be glad in you." 3.3. "We have loved your breasts more than wine."
Not the wine that is mixed by Christ, but that by whose drunkenness Noah formerly grew weak and which led Lot astray.
"More than this wine we have loved the outflowings of milk from your breasts." For the breasts given by Christ were those two commandments.
They gladden, not as though they merely weaken. Therefore the apostle too says: "Do not drink wine to excess in drunkenness." 3.4.
Now from this, beloved, it says: "We have loved your breasts more than wine," it says,
"righteousness has loved you," for those alone who follow righteousness are the ones who have loved you.
But the unbelievers have hated you and are liable before that Judge who repays.
"I am black and beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem": I have sinned, but still more I am beautiful, for Christ has loved me.
4.1. "I am black and beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem." All you nations, gather together and come and see me, this beloved one. 4.2.
"Do not marvel at this appearance of mine, that I am blackened, nor for this reason either, that the sun has looked on me darkly."
See the word of those who have gathered, who confessed what has passed: Do not look at this sinner, and for this reason too, that Christ has disregarded me.
And indeed he says this truly of the orb of the sun, for he says thus: "And to you who fear my name the sun of righteousness shall appear."
5.1. "Do not look at me, for I am blackened, nor for this reason, that the sun has overlooked me."
It overlooked her for this reason, because it trusted her, so that she might abide in repentance. 5.2.
For: "The sons of my mother became my attackers; those prophets kept calling me without giving offense, saying, 'Turn to the law of Moses.'" 5.3.
"They set me as keeper of the vineyard." They expected my ruin because of the reception of those who were coming. "My vineyard I could not keep."
And because I could not keep that people of mine; for that people of Israel is called a vineyard.
Come, Isaiah, bear witness whether you said: "The vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth is the house of Israel.
I stood and waited for it to yield grapes, and it yielded thorns." For this reason she says, "My vineyard I could not keep."
6.1. "Tell me, you whom my soul has loved." Tell me, Christ, give me an answer, I beg you: "Where do you pasture, where do you rest at midday?"
You have cast me off and left me. You have gone away to the Gentiles; I have remained an orphan. 6.2. I, this great one, have become desirous of poverty.
"Where do you pasture, where do you rest?" Let me not be disregarded, as one lost from the flock; may this not happen to me!
I who from the first received those who came, how should I now be [?] of the Gentiles?
7.1. At that very moment that voice of asking reached him, and Christ was revealed from there.
The voice with which he gives direction to that people. 7.2. "If you are not recognized, O beautiful one among women."
And this means: "If you do not turn with all your heart and confess your sins, so that you may be justified,
and if you do not become recognized as beautiful among women, you who boast and say, 'I am black and beautiful;
I have sinned, yet I am beloved,' that being loved is no help to you at all.
For since God is able even from stones to raise up children to Abraham, let not that promise made to the former fathers deceive you.
I have not shown partiality [?] to men, and now, if you do not know yourself and do not repent, behold, Abraham is saved,
but to you it will bring no benefit, for kinship with him is a help to the one in whom faith is found.
But let there be good works, so that there may be a choosing out of those righteous kin.
Therefore, if no one recognizes you, you beautiful one among women, 'go out and follow the track of the flocks and pasture your kids,' 7.3.
which means this: Follow me unshod and naked, for I have chosen out the choice sheep for myself, and you are counted among the kids, you who have been weighed over to the left.
But at my right hand I have counted those sheep. 7.4.
From now on Israel is no longer entrusted to you as a flock, for the white ones and the many-colored ones were Jacob's, and he separated them from the [?] ones.
For he assigns to Jacob that flock of his own, and those many-colored ones are Laban's.
Therefore the white, that is, the color of Jacob, and the many-colored, that of Laban, for it is one and the same: what had been marked is what has been [?] taught. 7.5.
But what is marked, that the unpleasant one [?] pastured.
"If you are not beautiful, you who are known among women, go out and follow in the tracks of the flock, and pasture your kids by the flock of the shepherds."
Now go to the Gentiles and become the likeness of all radiances. He calls that one of the kings a shepherd [?], to whom he went; it spread over the whole world.
"If you, that beautiful one, are not known among women, go out in the tracks of the flock."
8.1. "To my steed among the chariots of Pharaoh I have likened you, you who are near to me."
O great counsels, O truth, which has been rightly told to us! "If you turn back, O people, then I will reckon you as my own," he says.
As of my steed, which is harnessed to the chariots of Pharaoh. And in those times the steed was honored, and so were the chariots of Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians.
Just as this image, following one upon another, is glorious and beautiful, so you too will be beautiful if you repent. 8.2. And see further the new grace of the division.
For the steed was from the people, like those blessed apostles who were sent forth to run, like steeds in the world.
And the chariot is the assembly of the Gentiles, and the apostles are harnessed in the church to draw it rightly, by divine ordering, along the ascents of heaven.
And because the apostles are called steeds, the prophet says: "Send forth your prophets and stir up the many waters."
And again he says: "Mount your chariots, and your cavalry is the salvation of the world." 8.3.
But as for what he said, "Send forth your horses, stir up the many waters," this is the stirring up of many nations,
who, like waters stirred up by waves, were being shattered, who were stirred up by restlessness.
Now, pastured in the fold and knowing Christ, they are justified. 8.4.
O beautiful steeds, who have obtained the going of the righteous by their running, who built up nothing by the flash of the sword or by combat, but proclaimed the good news of everything in peace.
For these steeds are yoked to one another, neither turning aside from one another nor falling, in no way lagging behind in heart [?], and not throwing off the yoke. 8.5.
But behold, like tested animals submissive to the yoke, they draw many nations, like chariots, yoked for the sake of redemption.
Now those steeds, the twelve [?] righteous ones, have been found yoked and going straight forward.
Made firm by the harness [?] of love as by a strap, and submissive to the yoke of faith.
As if by four chariot wheels, they recounted the counsel of the journeying of the four evangelists;
they spread abroad the good Word, the guide of the chariot, and accomplished the course for the sake of righteousness,
through the twelve, for the building up of the world, they appointed all nations for him [?], like stirred-up waters. 8.6.
O the blessedness of those blessed steeds, for these had the wheels, as among wheels, for this new gospel was harnessed to the old law.
But now the chariots too are very beautiful, for they were depicted in many forms.
For with them were the lion and the vine, the vineyard, and the man and the eagle. O the diverse form of the new Gospel, yoked with the righteous chariots!
For its lion was as a king, proclaimed by Matthew the evangelist. And the vine was as the vineyard of the high priest, proclaimed by Luke.
And its man was as the one who suffered, expressed by Mark, and its eagle too was as the Word, sent flying up to heaven by the blessed John.
Through this thought, the thought of that preaching abroad was made known. 8.7.
Following this chariot are the wheels of the cart, which did not turn back on their track, for in those chariots was the spirit of the miracle.
For it has been told to us by Ezekiel. For in the Gospel, too, was that spirit full of many eyes, through the calling of diverse nations by the commandments. 8.8.
Now this is the righteous one among the steeds, and for this reason he cries out and says: "To my steed among Pharaoh's chariots I have likened you, my near one."
Repent, O congregation, so that you too may preach about Christ; become like a steed, to run swiftly through the world as Paul did, and a shepherd as Peter did,
so that you may appear righteous through Christ, or as a blessed one among the disciples, so that you may seal yourself [?] with the inexpressible steeds. 8.9.
O the new counsels! For he gives a righteous reply, saying:
"To my steed I have likened you, among Pharaoh's chariots, you who have drawn near to me." If you repent, learn with what beauty you are to be adorned.
9.1. "For your cheeks have become beautiful like turtledoves," for you have the purple of faith, which makes you careful through the word. 9.2.
"Your neck is like that of the son of Seros [?]." For you have the boldness of nobility. You do not merely look with your head hung down, but high up toward heaven.
10.1. "May likenesses of gold be made for you from pendants of silver."
For of these, the one who was made faithful only in measure through the Law [?], but now the surpassing beauty of gold is established, and the Gospel. 10.2.
For from pendants of silver, likenesses of gold have been made for you, for he likens you to righteous men, who are like gold tested and purified.
11. "While the king is in his chamber." For Christ has come and arrived with kingship. "Nard has spread abroad its scent; a stored vessel for me is my beloved.
12.1. "My nard gave forth its fragrance." The ointment of grace was spread abroad, so that the circumcision too might be able to be saved: the vessel of perfumed ointment, Christ,
strengthened by the clothing of the flesh, by the cord of love, so that because of this, like a crushed cluster [?]. 12.2.
"My beloved has settled among my bridal chambers [?]."
For he was anointed of the Law and the Gospel: "a vessel of perfumed ointment is my beloved; he shall dwell between my breasts."
13.1. "Nard, like that of Cyprus, is my beloved in the vineyard of Engedi."
O the beauty of Cyprus, by the hand [?], by which the anointing was adorned, so that the vineyard of Engedi might rightly be reckoned as such.
Engedi is a place in the region of Judea, in which balsam is found. There are vineyards there, trained up on trees.
This, obtained by cutting [?] from those trees, gives forth that ointment. Now he would say: "The little kinsman in the vineyard of Engedi."
He makes this known to us: he was mighty upon the tree through suffering, and by [?] in the side upon the tree he sends forth fragrance, like that of balsam.
As the word went forth from his mouth, so Christ gave forth his fragrance. 13.2.
But, beloved, as long as those fruits stand upon the tree in the vineyard, until they are crushed, they do not give forth their fragrance.
But when it is pruned by the craftsman with a blade, then at once and quickly it sheds tears; for Christ too at that time wept over the people,
for he was able to spread fragrance upon them by openly giving help, for upon that tree he was wounded in that vineyard,
so that he might show us the good fragrance of ointment. 13.3. And since the Word, beloved,
moreover dwelt in the flesh, and since the great one appeared as if humbled, so that he might be made manifest;
and he showed the new grace of distribution. The rich one became poor for us, so that we might be made rich by his riches.
So from now on, beloved, this one, hung on the tree, appeared as the good fragrance of ointment.
For he humbled himself, and the Word, raised upright, sang forth, and at that time the fragrance, spread abroad, filled them,

so that the mercy of distribution might further appear, through the continual spreading of the fragrance of ointment, for gladdening; for he came forth from the heart of the Father and brought good news to the earth. 13.4.
He himself was lifted up from the earth and appeared like the fragrance of ointment and hastened up to heaven; he who had been spread down from heaven went up from earth to heaven.
For the fruit-bearing dew came down from on high, so that these earthly ones might be sealed for life, which is this:
the Word came down, so that men might be able to ascend to heaven.
This likeness of the figures is shown by the words: "My little kinsman in the vineyard of Engedi."
14.1. And immediately he answers and says: "Behold, I am beautiful, my close one, behold, I am beautiful."
To this he answers further: "But confess me well; for this reason all the more will I confess you beautiful." 14.2.
What then is it that Christ says, namely, "You are beautiful," if not on account of "Take heart, daughter, your sins are forgiven you"?
15.1. He answered further and said: "Behold, I am good, my little kinsman, and beautiful," for I am beloved of all, even of those who do not know you.
For at that time those who did not know were taught by Christ. Then, understanding well, they would believe.
And he said: "O, this man is someone wise and great, and it is not known that he is God!" Now from now on, O men, understand what lies before us. 15.2.
"Behold, I am beautiful, my little kinsman, and comely too, you who cool my bed."
What does he intend to say about his dwelling? For he says: "You who cool well upon the bed."
He makes known to us that grace of the heart, which cools all those whom burning heat befalls, 15.3.
For just as those who flee from the heat to shady places, to rest beneath them, so also all who are held fast by sin,
hasten eagerly to that shade of Christ, so that they may attain the shade of the Holy Spirit. "Upon our bed, giving pleasant shade."
16.1. "The hands [beams?] of our houses are of fir trees." Now who are these, if not the fathers?
For just as the fir does not rot, so the glory of the fathers is not hidden. 16.2.
"Our rafters are of cypress." For the rafter bears the whole structure.
O beloved, the bloom of the cypress never fails, but it keeps its same appearance forever and stays the same in summer and in winter.
So also the apostles never diminish; they are the rafters and the strengthening of the churches.
And it has the power of the Holy Spirit in its capacity, and whatever is upon it, it is able to hold. "Our rafters are of cypress."
17.1. From here on he begins to praise himself with justification, and he says:
"I am a flower of the field," for it is not spread over the breadth of the earth, for through faith in you, behold, I am a flower to all people.
And this is fitting, for when someone from among the circumcised believes in Christ and appears like a flower, he is capable of both the old and the new. 17.2.
"I am a flower, like a lily of the valleys and like a lily among thorny places."
O the manifest thoughts of that righteous mouth, which appear in these parables!
For he says: "I am a flower of the field, like a lily in the valleys and like a lily among the thorny place."
He shows us the fragrance of the lily as a figure of the saints, for just as the lily brings forth a brilliant beauty, so also righteous deeds shine and bloom in the valleys.
So also the graces grow toward those who have been humbled, and, as among thorns in the land, they do not [?] from deeds. 17.3.
And the varied form, like the form of the lily, he has shown us as a figure of truth.
He reveals himself, for there is also the color of gold in it, for by burial, through hands, it was taken out with adornment and held,
like the flesh of Christ, guarded by the Spirit, or else those whose hands were defiled by unbelief,
but whoever believes will rejoice in the fragrance of his ointment. For the color of gold is also mingled with the white.

For in the Spirit he shows us the suffering of the flesh, so that the thought of its spreading abroad may appear through the confession of all the righteous and through the gaining of the brilliance of the Spirit.
"I am a flower of the field, like a lily of the valleys and like a lily among the thorny place."
18.1. Now to those who have received this fragrance he says: "Behold, I am beautiful, my close one," and again he says: "Behold, I am beautiful."
And this is said concerning Christ: "And behold, I am made fair, my kinsman [literally: sister's son], like an apple among the trees of the forest." 18.2.
For just as, beloved, a fragrance comes forth from the apple more than from all fruits,
So too Christ, among all the prophets, hung upon the tree, gave forth fragrance as of an apple.
19.1. And it says: "Behold, my beloved kinsman answers me and says: Draw near, my close one and my beauty, my little dove, my perfect one."
Now truly he speaks of this dove as one brought close, for he calls her with eagerness and says: "Come to me, all you who are weary and heavy-laden."
Now who is this heavy-laden one, if not those synagogues to whom he was speaking? 19.2. He calls this one close by the grafting.
And now what is this grafting, beloved, if not something like being set beside a right [?] wall? For that wall is a refuge before him.
Come, draw near to me in the Gospel, so that you may be found equal to the righteous through that close grafting. 19.3.
"Show me your face and let me hear your voice, for your face is gentle and your voice is beautiful." "Show me your face and let me hear your voice."
Boldly show your Christianity by sealing yourself on the forehead. "Let me hear your voice." Confess the truth by speaking it aloud.
"Show me your face and let me hear your voice, for it is gentle and sweet": the voice of the one who has confessed Christ. And beautiful is the face of the one who has boldness from him.
20.1. And he answers and says: "Catch for us the foxes that destroy the vineyards, for our vineyards are in flower." O blessed voice, O truth dispensed in righteousness,
by whose hand the heretics are seized! Catch for us the little foxes while they are still young;
take care that they do not become full-grown and fill the vineyards with their guile while they are in flower.
He says this by way of teaching. For when he says, "Catch for us the little foxes," he is saying nothing other than this:
"Remove heresy from among you," so that the burnt offering [?] may appear pure, if you wish to understand, O man; for he calls the heretics foxes.
For those false prophets were nothing other than heretics.
For those who teach what is false and preach falsehood are heretics, for Jeremiah cries out and says:
"Behold, your false prophets, O Jerusalem, are like foxes shut up in a hole."
And again Christ himself answers Herod and says to him: "Tell that fox: Behold, today and tomorrow I accomplish works of power, and on the third day I shall be glorified." 20.2.
And what new plan Samson carried out against the foxes! For when his wife had been taken from him,
he caught three hundred foxes and tied them to one another, and fastened firebrands to the tails of them all, and burned all the grainfields and vineyards.
And this was a sign, for it gives the number, saying: "He tied three hundred foxes to one another," and in the end the kindled fire burned them up.
This shows us that they were heretics, for they confessed the sufferings of Christ as the three hundred; but they had not acquired the power. 20.3.
As for his tying tail to tail, this was to show what is dissimilar and conflicting, for they too are at odds with one another in their speech.
And there were lit torches on their tails, for the judgment at their end is a consuming fire. 20.4.
Now for this reason the Spirit says: "Catch for us the little foxes that destroy the vineyards."
which — I [mean?] the vineyards [?] — but that vineyard which was newly planted and, while still in flower, was about to yield fruit,
it ruins and destroys and tears down; does it not have power, so that the cluster and the ripe fruit may be gathered by Christ? "Now our vineyards are in bloom."
21.1. She answers and says to him: "Behold, the beloved has arrived leaping, and has come."
O blessed voice! For when afterward there is to be vengeance for that vineyard, so that those foxes may be caught, she rightly cries out and says:
"Behold, my beloved has arrived leaping upon the tops of the mountains, to leap across upon the hills."
"My beloved is like a gazelle and its fawn upon the ravines of the mountains, my bed." 21.2. O the dispensation of new grace!
O those very great counsels! "'Behold, my beloved has arrived leaping, and has come,' it says." What then is the meaning of that leaping?
He leapt down from heaven into the womb of the Virgin; he leapt up from the holy womb onto the tree; he leapt from the tree
into hell; he leapt up from there in this human flesh to the earth. O the new resurrection! Then he leapt up from earth to heaven.
He is seated at the right hand of the Father, and he will afterward leap down to earth to render recompense. 21.3.
"Behold, lo, this one has arrived leaping upon the top of the mountains, to leap down upon the hills," for those
who think lofty thoughts — he will not set his foot upon them, but passes by them with a leap, not stopping with them.
22.1. "My beloved is like a gazelle and its fawn," for the swiftness of his word, renewed and light, was preached upon [?].
See, O man, how light that course was: from the east he appeared in the west, and from the west he was found to have reached the south;
from the south, shown to be trustworthy within that virgin chariot. 22.2. See the courses of righteousness: he went down to the underworld and hastened up to heaven.
For he did not remain in the darkness of this earth, but, shown forth as light, he went up to heaven.
And then again, having flown up, shining forth like a great star and shown forth as the sun of righteousness, he is glorified at the thrones of the Father. 22.3.
O the strength and great swiftness of that course! Already from youth he outran all, so that at one time as a gazelle and at another as a stag he might show the swiftness of his feet.
Now see Christ, at one time as a gazelle, swift in running, and at another as a stag with beautiful horns.
And both have cloven hooves and chew the cud. 22.4. And this the holy Law shows us clearly, for purity was made manifest;
Christ makes manifest the faith of the two laws, and always praises the firmness of the Law and the Gospel,
by the promise of his manifest and pure word he spread over [?], on account of which he says thus: "Behold, my beloved has become like a gazelle and its fawn."
23.1. Again she cries out: "Behold, my beloved looks through the window, peers down through the lattice, my beloved:
Come, my near one, beautiful one and dove." O that new proclamation!
And then that soul cries out openly, with sincerity: "My beloved looks down through the window."
But now, of which windows does he speak? Come, stand forth, prophet, bear witness and say: "Windows were opened in the heavens."
And of which window does he speak, if not that of the prophets, through whom the word, gushing forth, has flowed out in every direction from here?
23.2. "Through the window he looks out at me and says to me: Come, my near one, come."
Therefore it is to be understood that through all the prophets he cries out and says: "Draw near to me."
Come, stand forth, O blessed Elijah, bear witness. Rightly you said to Israel: "How long will you not cease limping on both feet?"
Draw near, come, my near one, come quickly, quickly, my perfect dove, come: this is what he signifies to us.
24.1. For this reason she again cries out and says: "By night I sought him whom my soul loved; I sought him and did not find him. The watchmen who guarded the city found me.
One [?] whom my soul loved, and behold, now, as soon as I had gone away for a moment, I found him whom my soul loved.
I found him and will not let him go until I bring him to the house of my mother and to the treasure chambers of her who conceived me." 24.2.
O that blessed voice! O those blessed women of former times, shown forth beforehand as a type!
For this reason she cries out and says: "By night I sought him whom my soul loved." See this fulfilled in Martha and Mary.
With them the assembly earnestly sought Christ as one dead, not supposing him to be alive, for thus it signifies to us and says:
"By night I seek, and I found him whom my soul loved." 24.3.
The writings of the Gospel say: "The women came by night to seek the tomb." "I sought him and did not find him."
"Why do you seek the living one among the dead?" And no one of his own was found there, for the sepulcher was not his dwelling place, but the heavens.
Why do you seek on earth him who sits exalted on the thrones?
Why do you seek the most glorious of the glorious in a contemptible grave? Why do you seek the perfect one in the sepulcher?
Behold the stone rolled away; why do you seek in the grave him who, behold, is filled with grace in the heavens?
Why do you seek him who has been set free as though he were bound, and there, as though he were shut up in prison?
24.4. See a new counsel fulfilled there; for thus she groans and says: "I sought him and did not find him.
The watchmen who guarded the city found me." Who were they who found them, if not the angels who were sitting there?
And which city, if not the new Jerusalem, the flesh of Christ? "The watchmen who guarded the city found me."
These women ask: "Have you perhaps seen him whom the soul loved?" For they said to them: "Whom do you seek? Jesus the Nazarene? Behold, he is risen."
25.1. "And as soon as I had gone away from them for one moment." And as they turned back and went away, the Savior met them;
then was fulfilled what was said: "Behold, as soon as I had gone away for one moment, I found him whom my soul loved." 25.2.
But the Savior answered and said to them: "Martha! Mary!" And they said to him: "Rabboni," which is translated "my Lord."
"I found him, I loved him. And behold, I will [not ?] let him go." For at that time she holds firm by clasping his feet.
And he cries out to her: "Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father."
And she clung to him and said: "I will not leave you until I bring you in and make you enter into my heart."
"I will not leave him until I bring him into the house of my mother and into the chambers of her who conceived me in her womb."
The love of Christ, gathered within the womb, does not want separation; for this reason she says with a cry: "I found him and I will not let him go."
O blessed woman, who clung to his feet so that she might be able to fly up into the air! 25.3.
Martha and Mary were saying this to him. He showed Martha's intention beforehand through Solomon: "You do not have the power to fly up."
Ascend to the Father and offer a new sacrifice. Offer Eve, no longer led astray, but with her hands eagerly clinging to the tree of life.
Behold, I have clung to the knees, not like the edge of a net [?] that might be torn away. Rather, I have clung to the feet of Christ.
Do not cast me down upon the earth, lest I go astray; carry me up to heaven. O blessed woman, who does not want separation from Christ!
25.4. For this reason she says: "When I had gone from them only a moment, I found him whom my soul loved."

Take, my heart, mingle with the spirit, make it firm, bring it to perfection, so that the flesh too may be able to be joined to the heavenly things. Let this flesh of mine be mingled with that which is heavenly.
Drink, as wine; take up, lift up to heaven then a new cup, mixed, which desires to follow and not to go astray,
no longer dregs [?] strained out [?], and not touching the tree of knowledge. But here, from now on, vanquished through death upon the tree. 25.5.
Receive Eve, so that she may no longer give birth with groaning, for pains, groanings and sorrows have been driven away.
Receive from now on Eve, walking in good order; take and recognize this gift, which, held out to the Father, you offer anew: Eve no longer naked, the fig leaf no longer her clothing.
Rather, she is clothed by the Holy Spirit, for he has put on her a good garment, which has no corruption.
Christ was not held to be one stripped naked; although those linen cloths lay in the tomb, he was not naked.
For Adam too at first was naked, and a renewed adornment of sinlessness, gentleness and incorruption had been put on him,
having fallen away from which they were found naked; but now he is found openly clothed again. 25.6.
And after this the assembly confesses with a cry through these women.
They show us a good testimony, those who became apostles to the apostles, sent by Christ, to whom the angels had first said:
"Go and tell the disciples: He goes before you to Galilee; there you will see him."
But so that the apostles might not doubt because of the angels, Christ himself met those apostles,
So that the women might be apostles of Christ, and might by obedience fill up what was lacking in the old Eve.
From now on may she appear as one who listens in perfect obedience. 25.7. O new consolations! Eve is called an apostle.

Behold, from now on she has understood the [?] of the serpent and no longer goes astray, for the one she looked upon she has from now on come to hate, and she has counted as an enemy the one who led her astray through desire.
From now on that tree of error will no longer lead her astray. Behold, from now on she is made glad by that life, by the tree, by confession.
Through that tree she experienced taste from Christ; she became worthy of the good, and her heart desired food. 25.8.
From now on she will no longer hunger, nor will she hold out corruptible food to human beings; she has received incorruption.
From now on she is in unity and is a helper, for Adam leads Eve. O that good helper, through the good news brought as an offering to her husband!
For this reason the women brought the good news to the disciples. 25.9. And therefore they counted them as people in error, and on this account they doubted.
But the reason was this: that it was Eve's custom to tell of deception and not of truth.
"What then is this new telling of the resurrection, O women?" And that is why they counted them as people in error, so that they might appear not as deceivers but as speakers of truth.
At that time Christ appeared to them and said: "Peace be with you."
Teaching this by it: "I, who appeared to these women, also willed to send them to you, the apostles." 25.10.
Now, concerning these things that have happened: for, beloved, from now on, now, behold, he brings peace to the assembly, and the Church is glorified.
26.1. And what does it say? "Who is this who comes out of the wilderness, like billows of smoke rising up, a fragrance of incense sent forth,
myrrh and frankincense, with all the fragrances of the compounders?" O that new voice! O those wonderful discourses!
O Church that comes out of the wilderness, so that she may be a citizen with Christ: "Who is this who comes out of the wilderness?"
For the Gentiles had for a long time become a wilderness toward God.
But from now on, by the grace of God, she is counted as a citizen with the saints, since the Church is adorned and made manifest by the compounding of fragrant ointments. 26.2.
And it says: "Now who is this who comes out of the wilderness, like smoke of incense sent up?"
O that good incense, the fragrant incense compounded!
For as to its saying, "like fragrant smoke of incense sent up": smoke comes out of fire and rises into the air, and the flame,
as if it were a guide of chariots, it shows us, and it becomes visible. So too the good discourse of Christ, spread abroad and unceasing, rises from earth to heaven;
for it made beautiful incense spring up through the unceasing discourse of the resurrection, like billowing smoke of incense rising. 26.3.
For in this manner, in likeness to the obtaining of fragrance, it not only smokes there below, but also reaches up to heaven, like the flame of a fire burning incense.
"Myrrh and frankincense, by all the compounders." O again those very great discourses! O that true preaching!
For the myrrh becomes the proclaimer of the sufferings of Christ and of his burial.
And the incense is burned up for the glorifying of God, but it is wholly compounded by those who blend the perfumes.
And all the fragrance gathered together belongs to Christ, who is proclaimed by the commandments and the Gospel.
For this reason it cries aloud and says: "Myrrh and incense, from all the blenders of perfumes."
27.1. "Behold, the bed of Solomon, and sixty mighty men surrounding it, of the mighty men of Israel, each with a sword on his thigh, trained in combat."
O blessed countenance! O bed of rest!
For by the bed of Solomon it reveals no one else but Christ himself.
For just as someone weary, after much labor, climbs up to rest on a bed,
in order to rid himself of weariness through that rest, so we too, having turned from the vanity of this world, would rid ourselves of the burden,
the weight of sins that lay upon our shoulders; by falling down before Christ we find rest, as on a bed. 27.2.
In the same way all the generations of the fathers, who were able to inherit that perfect rest, were given rest by nothing else but by Christ.
O rest of good things, able to gather everything together by way of counsel!
This bed the Shunammite woman prepared for the blessed Elisha. On this bed the dead who were laid upon it rose again.
The son of the widow was granted back, and the child of the Shunammite woman was raised. 27.3.

This bed was being carried out uncovered, and before it had yet passed through the gate, Christ appeared, meeting it, showing forth his own resurrection, and he said with authority to those who had lifted it:
"Set down this burden, do not carry what you are not able to bear."
At once, as they set down the bed, he took the boy by the hand and gave him to the widow. 27.4.
On this same bed lay sick the daughter of the ruler, who was twelve years old.
At that time he entered the house in the presence of the witnesses and raised the girl. 27.5.
To this bed hastened the woman who for a long time had not been healed of the condition of women, and she touched the hem with her hand. 27.6.
Behold wondrous beds, for all who look upon this are shown forth as belonging to the true wedding, the changing of water into wine, by the sight of its taste.
O blessed bed, on which Abraham has been kept [?], on which Isaac is offered up,
on which Jacob is magnified, on which Moses became ruler, on which Aaron is the offerer of prayer!
27.7. O blessed children, who rightly inherited the inheritance of the fathers.
Behold the various beds, on which the sixty mighty ones have been made manifest; these beds they assigned as their own to the righteous generation of the fathers,
by the gathering of all the righteous to Christ, for he is brought forth from them all.
For the Scripture says: "Sixty mighty men around it, from the people of Israel," for out of all the people of Israel these mightiest ones are taken by selection,
who are shown to be fathers, who are able to gird the sword upon their thighs. And what then is the sword on the thigh, if not the Word,
who passed through among those fathers, having come forth from the loins, so that to him [?] who should be able to bring forth from the loins?
These are the sixty thousands, and this is no lie. 27.8.
For from Adam to Christ those sixty thousands are completed, resting upon that bed, through whom the Word has been spread abroad; it signifies to us the coming forth from those loins.
For this reason Abraham had the hands of the steward of his household placed upon his loins, for the Word was to come forth from those loins.
And Jacob, with an oath, had the hands of Joseph placed upon his thighs. 27.9.
O blessed loins, able to bring forth that blessed Word, whom the Father brings forth from his heart!
This one we see coming forth from those loins. Rightly the Word becomes the narrator of this revealed counsel,
and for these sixty fathers are completed from Adam to Christ, and the counsel of truth is openly handed down.
And the beds of Solomon are shown forth, 27.10.
for it was not that Solomon was a bed, but rather beds were shown forth by Solomon, so that the counsel of rest for all and the love transcribed on tablets of stone might be made manifest.
Behold the generation of the fathers handed down from the beginning of the world, the righteous generations shown forth, and what was kept silent by the fathers revealed,
and the bed of rest handed down. 27.11. And who then are these among the fathers? Come and let us see.
Now then, see: first Adam had Seth, and Seth had Enosh, and Enosh had Cainan, Cainan had Mahalalel, Mahalalel had Jared.
Jared had Enoch, Enoch had Methuselah, Methuselah had Lamech, Lamech had Noah, Noah had Shem, Shem had Arphaxad, Arphaxad had Shelah,
Shelah had Eber, Eber had Peleg, Peleg had Reu, Reu had Serug, Serug had Nahor, Nahor had Terah, Terah had Abraham, Abraham had Isaac,
Isaac had Jacob, Jacob had Judah, Judah had Perez, Perez had Hezron, Hezron had Aram, Aram had Amminadab, Amminadab had Nahshon, Nahshon had Salmon.
Salmon had Boaz, Boaz had Obed, Obed had Jesse, Jesse had David, David had Solomon, Solomon had Rehoboam, Rehoboam had Abijah,
Abijah had Asa, Asa had Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat had Joram, Joram had Uzziah, Uzziah had Jotham, Jotham had Ahaz, Ahaz had Hezekiah.
Hezekiah had Manasseh, Manasseh had Amos, Amos had Josiah. Josiah had Jeconiah and his brothers, who were removed from their homeland to Babylon.
And after their being carried captive to Babylon, Jeconiah begot Shealtiel, Shealtiel begot Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel begot Abiud, Abiud begot Eliakim, Eliakim begot Azor, Azor begot Zadok. Zadok begot Achim, Achim begot Eliud, Eliud begot Eleazar.
Eleazar begot Matthan, Matthan begot Jacob, Jacob begot Joseph. To Joseph was betrothed Mary the virgin. From her was born our Lord Jesus Christ. 27.12.
These are the holy couches, upon which he gathers the holy righteous ones, around which stand those sixty swordsmen, driving away that deceiver, so that he may not be able to approach them.
Upon this those from among the Gentiles are gathered, justified, at rest, glorifying God, whose is the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
